heroHeadline: Sheinbaum's Second Informe Claims 51% Homicide Drop as She Advances Dual-Nationality Ban and Anti-Corruption Overhaul
heroSubtitle: Mexico's 701-year national arc spans the founding of México-Tenochtitlán (1325), the Spanish Conquest (1521), 300 years of colonial New Spain, the Independence War (1810–1821), the Reform era and French Intervention, the Porfiriato (including Yaqui ethnic cleansing 1899–1908), the Mexican Revolution (1910–1920), seven decades of PRI hegemony, and the democratic transition of 2000. Today, President Claudia Sheinbaum — Mexico's first female president, 68% approval per El Financiero — delivered her Second Government Report on September 1 claiming a 51% homicide decline since taking office, is pushing a constitutional bill to bar dual nationals from the presidency and governorships, and has sent a two-law, 19-amendment anti-corruption package to Congress, all while the CJNG succession crisis (Day 198 since El Mencho's killing) and a stalled fourth round of USMCA review talks in Washington continue to test her government.
footerNote: Comprehensive national intelligence dashboard aggregating Mexico's full historical arc from 1325 to present. Data sourced from INEGI, Banxico, SESNSP, SEDENA, SRE, OHCHR, InSight Crime, and major international outlets.
